name: Saul and Doeg at Nob
charge: Slaughter of the priests of the Lord on an Edomite’s report
summary: Saul had set an Edomite over his servants. Doeg reported that Ahimelech had enquired of the Lord for David, given him the hallowed bread and the sword of Goliath, and Saul, who by then read any loyalty to David as treason against himself, would not hear the priest’s defence. The king’s own footmen would not put forth their hand against the priests of the Lord, so he got the Edomite to do what his own men would not: Doeg slew eighty-five men that wore a linen ephod and smote Nob, the city of the priests, with the edge of the sword. David wrote the Edomite’s sentence in a psalm.
offenseFull: David came to Nob to Ahimelech the priest, three days out in the field and fearful of king Saul, and the priest gave him hallowed bread, for there was no bread there but the shewbread that had been taken from before the Lord (1 Samuel 21:6-7). Christ recounted this very history when the Pharisees challenged his disciples for plucking the ears of corn on the sabbath day, asking whether they had never read what David did when he had need and was an hungred (Mark 2:25-26); precept it in your bibles if it is not there already. A certain servant of Saul was detained before the Lord that day: Doeg, an Edomite, the chief of Saul’s herdmen (1 Samuel 21:7). The scriptures tell us never to trust an enemy (Ecclesiasticus 12:10), yet here is a king of Israel with an Edomite set over his servants. Doeg answered and reported that he had seen the son of Jesse come to Nob to Ahimelech the son of Ahitub, who enquired of the Lord for him, gave him victuals, and gave him the sword of Goliath the Philistine (1 Samuel 22:9-10). Saul sent for Ahimelech and all his father’s house, the priests in Nob, and charged them with conspiracy; Ahimelech answered that no one among all the king’s servants was as faithful as David, the king’s son in law, who went at his bidding and was honourable in his house, and that it was hardly the first time he had enquired of God for him, and the king should impute nothing to his servant nor to all his father’s house (1 Samuel 22:13-16). Saul had become so desperate that he read loyalty to David as betrayal of himself, because he wanted everybody against David. That is no new thing under the sun: men put slander out to turn whole congregations against a man they have never sat down with and broken bread with.
judgmentFull: The king told the footmen standing about him to turn and slay the priests of the Lord, because their hand also was with David, but the servants of the king would not put forth their hand to fall upon the priests of the Lord. So the king said to Doeg, turn and fall upon the priests; and Doeg the Edomite turned and fell upon them and slew on that day fourscore and five persons that did wear a linen ephod, and smote Nob, the city of the priests, with the edge of the sword, both men and women, children and sucklings, oxen, asses and sheep (1 Samuel 22:13-19). Saul was able to get the Edomite to do what his own men would not do. Go back to Genesis and see the spirit that has been on this man from the beginning: Esau hated Jacob because of the blessing, and comforted himself with the purpose of slaying his brother (Genesis 27:41). That comfort in killing is the same thing seen in Doeg; when Saul appointed him to the task you can best believe he found pleasure in it. Eighty-five priests and a whole city destroyed because they showed affinity to David, all out of hatred and envy. The servant is not greater than his lord, and if they persecuted Christ they will persecute us (John 15:20), and not only by the heathen but by our own kinsmen.

One of the sons of Ahimelech, named Abiathar, escaped and fled after David, and told him that Saul had slain the Lord’s priests. David answered that he had known that day, when Doeg the Edomite was there, that he would surely tell Saul, and that he had occasioned the death of all the persons of his father’s house; Abiathar was to abide with him and fear not, for the man who sought David’s life sought his life, and with David he would be in safeguard (1 Samuel 22:20-23). Where the reigning king had become a threat, the fugitive became a shelter.

Doeg’s own sentence is written in the psalm David made about him, the psalm inscribed for the day when Doeg the Edomite came and told Saul that David was come to the house of Ahimelech: his tongue devised mischief like a sharp razor, working deceitfully, loving evil more than good and lying rather than speaking righteousness; therefore God would likewise destroy him for ever, take him away, pluck him out of his dwelling place, and root him out of the land of the living (Psalms 52:5). David did not tell the Edomite he could come and rule with him in the kingdom. That is the sentence, and it stands over the nation Doeg came from.

lawsResolved.text: Shedding of innocent blood is an abomination to God.
Government officers that engage in conspiracy, treachery and murder are to be put to death.
If a ruler hearken to lies, all his aides and ministers become wicked.
You shall not go about speaking slander or spreading false reports about others.
Doing injustice by justifying the wicked and condemning the righteous is an abomination and condemned by God.

text.text: So the priest gave him hallowed bread: for there was no bread there but the shewbread, that was taken from before the Lord, to put hot bread in the day when it was taken away.
Now a certain man of the servants of Saul was there that day, detained before the Lord; and his name was Doeg, an Edomite, the chiefest of the herdmen that belonged to Saul.
And he said unto them, Have ye never read what David did, when he had need, and was an hungred, he, and they that were with him?
How he went into the house of God in the days of Abiathar the high priest, and did eat the shewbread, which is not lawful to eat but for the priests, and gave also to them which were with him?
Now a certain man of the servants of Saul was there that day, detained before the Lord; and his name was Doeg, an Edomite, the chiefest of the herdmen that belonged to Saul.
Never trust thine enemy: for like as iron rusteth, so is his wickedness.
Then answered Doeg the Edomite, which was set over the servants of Saul, and said, I saw the son of Jesse coming to Nob, to Ahimelech the son of Ahitub.
And he enquired of the Lord for him, and gave him victuals, and gave him the sword of Goliath the Philistine.

And Saul said unto him, Why have ye conspired against me, thou and the son of Jesse, in that thou hast given him bread, and a sword, and hast enquired of God for him, that he should rise against me, to lie in wait, as at this day?
Then Ahimelech answered the king, and said, And who is so faithful among all thy servants as David, which is the king’s son in law, and goeth at thy bidding, and is honourable in thine house?

Did I then begin to enquire of God for him? be it far from me: let not the king impute any thing unto his servant, nor to all the house of my father: for thy servant knew nothing of all this, less or more.
And the king said, Thou shalt surely die, Ahimelech, thou, and all thy father’s house.

And Saul said unto him, Why have ye conspired against me, thou and the son of Jesse, in that thou hast given him bread, and a sword, and hast enquired of God for him, that he should rise against me, to lie in wait, as at this day?
Then Ahimelech answered the king, and said, And who is so faithful among all thy servants as David, which is the king’s son in law, and goeth at thy bidding, and is honourable in thine house?

Did I then begin to enquire of God for him? be it far from me: let not the king impute any thing unto his servant, nor to all the house of my father: for thy servant knew nothing of all this, less or more.
And the king said, Thou shalt surely die, Ahimelech, thou, and all thy father’s house.

And the king said unto the footmen that stood about him, Turn, and slay the priests of the Lord; because their hand also is with David, and because they knew when he fled, and did not shew it to me. But the servants of the king would not put forth their hand to fall upon the priests of the Lord.

And the king said to Doeg, Turn thou, and fall upon the priests. And Doeg the Edomite turned, and he fell upon the priests, and slew on that day fourscore and five persons that did wear a linen ephod.
And Nob, the city of the priests, smote he with the edge of the sword, both men and women, children and sucklings, and oxen, and asses, and sheep, with the edge of the sword.
And Esau hated Jacob because of the blessing wherewith his father blessed him: and Esau said in his heart, The days of mourning for my father are at hand; then will I slay my brother Jacob.
Remember the word that I said unto you, The servant is not greater than his lord. If they have persecuted me, they will also persecute you; if they have kept my saying, they will keep yours also.
And one of the sons of Ahimelech the son of Ahitub, named Abiathar, escaped, and fled after David.
And Abiathar shewed David that Saul had slain the Lord’s priests.
And David said unto Abiathar, I knew it that day, when Doeg the Edomite was there, that he would surely tell Saul: I have occasioned the death of all the persons of thy father’s house.
Abide thou with me, fear not: for he that seeketh my life seeketh thy life: but with me thou shalt be in safeguard.
God shall likewise destroy thee for ever, he shall take thee away, and pluck thee out of thy dwelling place, and root thee out of the land of the living. Selah.
